text:
Ottawa won 4-1, but the chance quality said this was a coin flip. The Senators generated 2.46 expected goals to Boston's 2.41, and in a simulation of every shot they deserved to win just 51 percent of the time. What separated the teams was the first 29 minutes, when OTT turned a modest edge into a four-goal lead that BOS never really threatened.

Tim Stützle did most of it. He scored a shorthanded snap shot at 7:39 of the first, worth only a 17 percent chance, then added another snap shot less than two minutes later on a 14 percent look. Drake Batherson made it 3-0 on a backhand 1:06 into the second, with Stützle collecting the assist, and Michael Amadio's snap shot at 5:19 made it 4-0. That was the best look of the lot at 23 percent. Ottawa led in expected goals through two periods, 2.17 to 1.55, but it was not a runaway, and Jeremy Swayman finished 1.54 goals worse than expected after allowing all four.

Boston carried the third, outchancing Ottawa 0.86 to 0.28, yet James Hagens' snap shot at 3:30 was a 2 percent chance and the only reward. Linus Ullmark preserved the margin, stopping all 10 shots for 1.55 goals saved above expected after Samuel Ersson was pulled. Neither team converted on four power plays, and BOS took 28 penalty minutes to OTT's 18.
